Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up — GPU sizing & throughput targets

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about ShopMetrics' plan for [insights generation] and the latency/throughput constraints you mentioned. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

- Usage profile you described: ~100M tokens/month to start, ramp to ~400–500M over 6–12 months; heavier generation on scheduled batch jobs plus some low-latency interactive queries.
- Throughput targets: want p95 latency <500ms for typical interactive flows; peak burst token throughput ~300–600 tokens/sec for batch pipelines.
- Preference: you mentioned wanting a cost-effective reserved option, possibly A100 for budget reasons but interested in H100 if perf gains justify it.

Action items for us:
1) We'll size a Dedicated offering (GPU type & count) to meet your peak throughput targets and provide estimated unit economics ($/1M tokens) under reserved pricing.
2) Please share a sample prompt set + typical response lengths for interactive vs. batch so we can generate a realistic token distribution.
3) Vendor/procurement timeline: Jason — you mentioned Q2 procurement target; can you confirm purchase window and any PO/contract requirements?

I've attached our Dedicated pricing deck and included a sample cost worksheet. Looping in Aditya and Logan for sizing notes — will follow up with an initial recommendation by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Expected token volumes: initial steady-state ~120M tokens/month, with fast-path batch runs pushing an extra ~150M in peak months. Plan to be at ~400M/mo at scale (9–12 months).
- Typical response lengths: interactive median ~60 tokens; batch generation averages ~800 tokens per call.
- Latency targets: interactive p95 ideally <300ms, p50 <150ms. Batch latency less critical but need throughput for scheduled windows.
- Budget: we're targeting an OPEX range of $40k–$70k/month for the Dedicated service initially.
- Unit economics target: look to be around $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens (including reserved discounts & expected caching).
- GPU preference: open to H100 for performance if it fits the budget; mentioned A100 as lower-cost option.
- Procurement: looking to approve in mid-June; procurement needs are standard PO + SOW, likely a 12-month committed term.

We'll upload a 7-day sample prompt bundle to the Drive link you shared by EOD. Happy to hop on a quick call with your infra folks if that helps.

—Sarah

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing follow-up — GPU sizing & throughput targets

Marissa / team — initial sizing notes below (high level):

- Recommended starting configuration: 2 x H100 80GB reserved nodes. Rationale: for mixed interactive (60 token median) + batch (800 token avg) this gives strong headroom for parallelism and KV cache. H100 provides ~20–30% perf improvement for long-context generation vs A100, which helps the batch windows and reduces per-token latency for interactive flows.

- Throughput estimates (approx):
  * Interactive — with smart batching and prefix caching, a 2x H100 cluster should comfortably hit >350 tokens/sec sustained with p95 <300ms for 8–12 concurrent interactive sessions.
  * Batch — scheduled generation distributing across the two GPUs should support ~700–1,200 tokens/sec aggregate during peak windows (depends on sequence lengths and model).

- Unit economics (ballpark):
  * Reserved-cost blended estimate: $850–$1,150 per 1M tokens (this factors in reserved discounts, expected caching hits ~10–20%, and batching benefits for throughput).
  * If ShopMetrics opts for A100 reserved nodes instead, estimate moves to ~$1,000–$1,350 per 1M tokens (cheaper HW but lower perf increases batch runtime; net unit cost can go up due to longer runtimes).

- Procurement-friendly plan: recommend 12-month reserved with 2x H100 baseline + auto-burst policy to spin up additional capacity for quarterly batch peaks (billed on usage). That should keep base OPEX in the $45k–$65k/month range depending on exact model and SLOs.

Caveats / notes:
- Exact numbers depend heavily on model family (decoder-only vs. mix), context window sizes, and tokenization. If you can share a 7-day sample as mentioned, we'll run a micro-benchmark and give a tighter cost per 1M tokens.
- If latency requirements tighten (p95 <200ms), we'll likely need 4x H100 or a split architecture (interactive on H100s, batch on A100s).

I'll run a quick internal benchmark once we have sample prompts. Happy to demo a micro-benchmark next week.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
